content.thinking:
I'm putting the postmortem together from the key facts: the cached spend totals went stale, so shoppers saw account pages missing recent purchases. Customer loss was none, and no deploys, flags, logs or metrics pointed to a change.

Now I'm working out the causal chain, starting from the symptom and moving toward why the cached figures stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger.

I'm weighing which thread to follow: the cache feed stopping up to date, or the page never checking entries against the account. Since no change is on record, I'm considering the page's missing check as a contributing factor rather than the trigger, but I still need to work out what the root cause is.

I'm weighing whether the root cause is the cache feed going stale from A5, with the record not showing why, or the page's missing check against the account. The page check would have stopped this even with the cache stall unchanged, so I'm treating it as a contributing factor and leaning toward the stall as the cause.

I'm settling on the cache feed stall as the thing that set this off, with the page's missing account check as a contributing factor the fix will cover. For the change that started it, I'm ruling out deploys, releases and flag changes on the service in the window I read, since none came back.

I'm checking the timing next: the cache stopped keeping up at A5 and the stale entries started being served from A6, which is what the record says even if the gap looks odd. I'm laying out the causal chain step by step, beginning with shoppers seeing spend totals that left out their recent purchases.

I'm laying out the next step of the chain: the stale copies were the whole of what was wrong, and the cached copies had stopped picking up new purchases from A5. The record shows nothing that changed at that point, and what stopped the updates isn't shown either, since the metrics and logs came back empty. I'm also noting the account page's missing check as the contributing factor that let stale entries through.

I'm going through the two contributing factors now: the account page serving cached entries without checking them against purchases it already had loaded, which the fix will cover, and a gap in watching whether the cache's updates were keeping up, since staleness began at A5 but the alert only fired after stale figures reached shoppers at A6.

I'm listing the remaining contributing factors now: the missing on-call paging for this alert, which meant no one was pulled in to look into why the cache feed stopped, and that stalled feed is still unrepaired.

I'm weighing whether the two remaining gaps belong among the contributing factors, and I'm settling on treating the unreadable metrics and empty logs as a detection gap, since an investigator who could read them might have found why the feed stopped.

I'm splitting the action item for the stalled cache feed into two parts: restoring its updates now as a mitigation, and separately tracking the risk that the figures go stale again while nothing is yet done to prevent it.

I'm drafting the action items now, starting with restoring the io-summary-cache update feed so cached spend figures keep up with the purchase ledger, and separately finding what stopped its updates from A5. I'm also adding a short-term step to rerun the stale-cache check and discard the entries it names until the feed is back, and I'm planning an alert on the cache's update lag against the purchase ledger.

I'm drafting the remaining action items: the stale-entry check could go on showing shoppers totals that miss their latest purchases, and I'm also adding a step to route the stale-figures alert to on-call paging and to make the io-shop metrics and logs readable.

I'm settling the root cause in plain terms: the io-summary-cache stopped applying new purchases to its cached spend entries from A5, so those entries fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct. The record doesn't show why the updates stopped, and the account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, most likely because they never checked a copy against the purchases first.

I'm listing what went well: the Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures, and the store's report of what it removed confirmed the fix. The alert also named the stale entries and noted that the purchase ledger never moved. I'm also noting the Code-Fix Agent's draft PR #528.

I'm noting that the mitigation only discarded the entries that disagreed when the alert's check ran, and nothing I've seen restarted the cache's updates, so the copies could go stale again. That's a gap in what was left behind after the fix, so I'm treating it as a went-wrong point.

I'm checking the assumptions behind the draft: that the stale figures were served from A6 as the alert states, which I'm taking from the alert's statement since no page views were counted, and that discarding the stale entries leaves the pages to rebuild from the purchase ledger.

I'm checking the wording of the code-fix note, making sure the claim about the page's lookup stays tied to what the reading showed and doesn't go past it. I'm also lining up the citations for the causal chain, so the step about the account page points back to the alert and the timed item it relies on.

I'm settling on the wording of the pull request note, keeping it free of a number and leaving the module name as it is.

action_items.item: Restore io-summary-cache's updates so cached spend figures take in new purchases again.
Until the cache's updates are restored, re-run the stale-figure check and discard the entries it names.
Find out what stopped io-summary-cache from taking in new purchases from {A5}, including any change made to io-summary-cache itself.
Add an alert that fires when io-summary-cache's updates fall behind the purchase ledger, whether or not stale entries are being served yet.
Route CachedSpendTotalsAreStale to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.
Make io-shop's per-minute metrics readable to the Investigator Agent.
Make io-shop's log lines readable to the Investigator Agent, or find out why none came back for the hours before the alert.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that left out purchases they had made. The purchases themselves were recorded correctly.

The pages were serving cached copies of the spend figures from io-summary-cache that had fallen behind the purchase ledger, while the ledger itself stayed correct. These stale cached copies were the whole of what was wrong.

ruled_out.what: A deploy, release or flag change on the service. None came back over the day before the alert, a window that covers the moment the copies stopped keeping up.
A flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before the flag history was read. The flag provider showed none.

causal_chain.step: The cached copies stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}. The oldest purchase that no stale figure counted was recorded then. What stopped the updates is not shown: the Investigator Agent got back no metrics and no log lines for the service.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's running spend total, and these copies stopped being updated with new purchases for a reason the record does not show; account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it.

contributing_factors.factor: Code-Fix read src/io_shop/account_page.py, and nothing ran that reading. In it, the account page's `_the_figure_for` serves any entry the cache returns without comparing the entry's purchase count with the purchases the page has already loaded for that account. So a stale entry kept being served for as long as the cache could be reached.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Pages would have treated an entry with a mismatched purchase count as a miss and worked the figure out from the purchases, so shoppers would not have been shown stale totals even with the cache's updates stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing was seen watching whether io-summary-cache's updates kept up with the purchase ledger. The copies stopped keeping up at {A5}, and the only thing that found it was the stale-figure check, once stale figures were being served.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The stopped updates could have been caught and dealt with before any stale figure reached a shopper.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person could have taken up the stopped cache updates, which the discarding of entries did not touch, and so shortened how long figures kept going stale.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No per-minute metrics and no log lines came back for the service when the Investigator Agent asked for them.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The investigation could have seen what stopped the cache's updates and put it right, rather than only clearing the entries that were stale at that moment.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The alert named each stale entry and pointed to a safe fallback: the purchase ledger, which never moved. That made it clear what to discard.
Argus read the flag provider's history to check for flag changes made by anyone else.
The Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures, which sent those pages back to the purchase ledger.
The Mitigation Agent judged the action confirmed against the store's own report of what it had removed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix to the account page as a draft pull request.

went_wrong: The mitigation discarded only the entries that disagreed when the alert's check ran. Nothing seen restarted the cache's updates, so the copies were left free to go stale again.

input.root_cause: The cached spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}, so they fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct. The evidence read does not show why the updates stopped.
input.still_at_risk: Cached spend figures that were not on the discarded list, and any that went stale later, could keep showing shoppers totals that leave out their latest purchases, and more would go stale each time a shopper bought again.
input.symptom: Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
